evidence_scope: analysis until E04; original E05 neither accessed nor used
style_goal: Source-grounded mechanics for future scene directions; avoid copying distinctive passages; focus on pacing, viewpoint, conversation and emotional continuity Every claim-versus-event contrast and multi-person visual scene requires evidence-granularity rather than a generic summary.

features.name: present_to_flashback_to_present
features.mechanic: Begin with a changed mental state; move backward to explain the trigger; return to present where memory has altered character behavior
features.writer_instruction: Signal both temporal boundaries; resolve an earlier external question without automatically resolving the inner conflict

features.name: ordinary_domestic_setup
features.mechanic: Everyday delivery, painting, tutoring, heat or chores supplies a practical reason for a meeting
features.writer_instruction: Establish what task all participants are performing before their relationship changes through dialogue

features.name: alternating_private_points_of_view
features.mechanic: Narrator alternates access to different private thoughts so readers understand misunderstandings characters cannot
features.writer_instruction: Each POV move must identify whose knowledge is available; do not transfer a private thought into another character's knowledge

features.name: rapid_dialogue_turns
features.mechanic: Short direct speaker turns, unfinished sentences, teasing corrections and repeated address create a conversational cadence
features.writer_instruction: Write clear speaker tags, interleave visible reactions after a meaningful turn; do not replace interaction with a narratorial conclusion

features.name: pronounced_punctuation_and_interjections
features.mechanic: Frequent ellipses, elongated vocatives and colloquial expressions reflect informal, breathy dialogue pacing
features.writer_instruction: Borrow functional rhythm rather than identical wording; differentiate how each participant hesitates or reacts

features.name: author_explains_emotional_contrast
features.mechanic: Narration explicitly compares current behavior with earlier self-image, uncertainty and self-correction
features.writer_instruction: Attach one before/after thought to each major new decision, citing the prior episode state in the director metadata

features.name: character_role_contrast
features.mechanic: Bantu's extroverted framing contrasts with Bobby's sparse but increasingly direct requests; Dhika responds differently to each
features.writer_instruction: Do not merge the two pupils' motivations; give each distinct line count, conversational tactic and response

features.name: setups_and_callbacks
features.mechanic: Later scenes refer to earlier objects, clothing, discussions or accidents and thereby make incremental changes legible
features.writer_instruction: Every callback must point to its prior source event; record whether it creates action, inner realization or unresolved topic

features.name: descriptive_lens_not_automatic_action
features.mechanic: Narratorial visual descriptions and comparisons channel an observer viewpoint, but don't independently imply body contact
features.writer_instruction: Keep observer, object of attention, figurative detail and actual behavior in separate fields

features.name: embarrassment_comedy_reassurance_cycle
features.mechanic: Awkwardness rises, a misunderstanding or joke permits a response, then ordinary task resumes, while private doubts linger
features.writer_instruction: Give each character a separate before/after reaction; do not overstate closure

features.name: intra_episode_time_jumps
features.mechanic: Time labels and abrupt next-day transitions compress routine hours while preserving one important unresolved emotional thread
features.writer_instruction: Log where participants are and which unfinished conversation or practical task carries to the next day

features.name: end_on_question_or_unpaid_reaction
features.mechanic: A scene stops at a physical observation or verbal question before the other character responds; next episode may use immediate scene continuation or a retrospective opener
features.writer_instruction: Store explicit cliffhanger condition: last act, who must respond, setting, what information is withheld, and permitted next-transition alternatives

features.name: separate_dialogue_label_from_narrated_visual_fact
features.mechanic: The narrator specifies the visible event, a speaker later uses a stronger label, and another speaker disputes the literal label. These are three different evidence classes, not one physical action.
features.writer_instruction: Record visible event separately from the spoken claim or question. Preserve the source-supported degree of exposure and the explicit correction. Do not equate a question with a confirmed event.

character_specific.dhika: Corrects how her appearance is characterized; reaction can differ from narration.
character_specific.bantu: Uses a provocative label and later backs away from its literal wording.
character_specific.bobby: Speaks and observes independently rather than automatically sharing Bantu's interpretation.

features.name: single_scene_actor_observer_response_triplet
features.mechanic: A chosen adjustment changes the visible context; another character notices; the first character observes the attention and forms a new private interpretation. No one participant's perspective is equivalent to all three beats.
features.writer_instruction: Create separate IDs for initiating gesture, what each observer notices, immediate spoken/visible response, and mental reaction. Cite each local source line and link IDs in temporal order.

character_specific.dhika: Choice, self-consciousness, observation of another's gaze and immediate verbal response must be individually indexed.
character_specific.bantu: Spoken confidence and tactics are distinct from actually observed behavior.
character_specific.bobby: Quiet visual attention and shorter statements are separate from Bantu's strategy.
character_specific.chotu: Private interpretation of visual attention must not be silently transferred into Dhika's knowledge.

dhika.narration: Expressive inner monologue with questions, sudden self-consciousness, playful speech, and rapid emotional reversal
dhika.dialogue: Uses familiar affectionate addresses and interjections; may turn from teasing to embarrassment or reassurance
dhika.continuity: Keep independent decisions and reactions distinct; a prior playful act does not settle every future choice

chotu.narration: Concrete practical concerns, incomplete experience, protective sense of responsibility
chotu.dialogue: Brief polite replies, misunderstandings and apologies, more hesitant after surprising exchanges
chotu.continuity: Never silently transfer Dhika's private thoughts to him

bantu.dialogue: Outgoing, humorous, request-driven, asks follow-up questions
bantu.continuity: Differentiate initiated conversation from actual granted request

bobby.narration: Reserved outward appearance and gradually growing ability to speak up
bobby.dialogue: Fewer words, direct requests emerging at conspicuous moments
bobby.continuity: His quieter responses and reassurance must not be copied from Bantu

john.narration: Domestic/family baseline and prior relationship history
john.continuity: Preserve what he has and has not actually been told

execution_principles: An action label is never a substitute for a scene beat
Do not invent historical contact as previously established
Distinguish deliberately chosen clothing, inadvertent change and other participants' interpretation
Dialogue must include misunderstanding or consequence as needed, not only 'teasing'
For an unresolved ending, carry forward the exact actor/question and opportunity for immediate reply
Keep all interpretations linked to source anchors, separate from raw text
